# My-lawyer

> AI-powered contract drafting platform built for corporate counsel across MENA jurisdictions. Drafts contracts in Arabic, grounds every clause in the controlling civil code or labour law, and exports a bilingual Arabic / English document with the language-prevailing clause auto-appended.

My-lawyer covers eleven Arabic-language jurisdictions: Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman, Jordan, Lebanon, Tunisia, and Libya. Each jurisdiction has its own indexed legal corpus and a curated bilingual translation glossary. Civil-law terminology is locked across the document — `حسن النية` always renders as "good faith" (in the civil-law sense), `الحصص` as "quotas (LLC)" not "shares", `الفسخ` as "judicial rescission" not "termination".

Every clause cites its controlling article. Citations are verified against a live snapshot of the source statutes. Unverifiable citations are flagged, never silently shipped.

## Jurisdictions

- [Egypt (EG)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/EG) — Egyptian Civil Code (Law 131/1948), Companies Law 159/1981, Labour Law 12/2003
- [Saudi Arabia (SA)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/SA) — Civil Transactions Law (Royal Decree M/191 of 1444H), Companies Law 1437H
- [UAE (AE)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/AE) — Civil Transactions Law (Federal Law 5/1985), Companies Law (Federal Decree-Law 32/2021)
- [Kuwait (KW)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/KW) — Civil Code (Decree-Law 67/1980), Companies Law 1/2016
- [Qatar (QA)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/QA) — Civil Code (Law 22/2004), Companies Law 11/2015
- [Bahrain (BH)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/BH) — Civil Code (Decree-Law 19/2001), Companies Law 21/2001
- [Oman (OM)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/OM) — Civil Transactions Law (Royal Decree 29/2013)
- [Jordan (JO)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/JO) — Civil Code (Law 43/1976)
- [Lebanon (LB)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/LB) — Code of Obligations and Contracts (1932)
- [Tunisia (TN)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/TN) — Code of Obligations and Contracts
- [Libya (LY)](https://my-lawyer.test/jurisdictions/LY) — Civil Code (1953)

## What makes it different

- **Citation-grounded, not hallucinated**: Every clause cites the controlling article. Citations are verified against the source statute.
- **Arabic-first**: The Arabic version is the legally binding text. English is the working translation, prepared for non-Arabic-reading parties.
- **Civil-law aware**: Civil-law concepts (good faith, judicial rescission, force majeure, quotas) are translated by their civil-law meaning, not their common-law cognate.
- **Region-specific**: Eleven jurisdictions, each with its own civil code, companies law, labour law, and citation form. The drafter picks the right one based on governing-law clause.
- **Versioned and auditable**: Every revision is captured. Compare drafts clause by clause. Roll back when senior counsel disagrees.

## Audience

Corporate counsel, in-house legal teams, M&A lawyers, transactional attorneys, and law firms operating across MENA jurisdictions where the contract is filed, registered, notarized, and litigated in Arabic.
